honesty.statement: Screenshots render the real plugin components and SDK primitives in a browser component harness. The plugin targets stock Hermes Desktop; optional provider metadata is capability-detected and shown as unavailable with provider dashboard links when absent. These are not packaged-app screenshots or live provider reads.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — status-bar chip (sample data)
screenshots.caption: The status-bar chip is the always-on entry point. It shows the active provider and the governing subscription windows, not a private chat quota.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — current provider popover (sample data)
screenshots.caption: Clicking the chip opens the current provider’s detail popover: every governing window, reset time, and any paid fallback balance.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — running agents footer (sample data)
screenshots.state: Popover footer · verified pool and unknown account
screenshots.caption: The footer attributes only what the gateway can prove. A child with a matching account shows the shared pool (5h 62%); a mismatched or missing account shows an em dash instead of borrowing another account’s balance.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — full page, multiple providers (sample data)
screenshots.state: Full page · subscription and credit providers
screenshots.caption: The full page keeps subscription windows and credit balances together: the active Codex allowance, OpenRouter API credit (opened to show its labelled sample balance), DeepSeek API credit, OpenCode Go, and Ollama Cloud. The xAI row stays unavailable — stock Hermes 0.23.1 has no xAI broker — and points at the official Grok dashboard instead of inventing credits.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — expanded active-provider metrics (sample data)
screenshots.caption: When an adapter supplies them, the active card extends to activity, prompt-cache efficiency, and published token rates. Counters, rates, and requests here are sample values; not every provider returns every field.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — popular provider connection cards (sample data)
screenshots.state: Popular provider cards · Claude, Gemini, Z.ai
screenshots.caption: Three always-listed connection cards separate subscription quota from API billing. They report credential presence and supported read paths only; an unconnected card says so instead of showing an invented zero.

rendered_text_assertions: No balance or quota is inferred.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — available to connect cards (sample data)
screenshots.caption: Read-only JSON definitions that ship in the catalog appear as Available to connect and name the exact missing environment variable. A card is setup guidance, not a live account test.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — approval, blocked, unknown states (sample data)
screenshots.caption: Profile-local definitions stay untrusted until a human approves that exact content. Editing the file, a mismatched approval record, or an unrecognized backend state is shown explicitly; nothing is fetched or invented.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — invalid definition errors (sample data)
screenshots.caption: An invalid profile definition keeps its exact schema errors visible, so the fix is actionable instead of a silent empty card.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — narrow responsive pane (sample data)
screenshots.caption: At a 420px pane width the plugin’s own layout stacks meters and provider cards without changing the data or hiding a reset.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — banked reset summary (sample data)
screenshots.caption: The stock-native reset panel reads the active Codex account only. This is a fixture summary: 2 banked resets, 1 usable now, with provider-reported inventory. No reset was redeemed.

screenshots.title: Provider Usage — reset confirmation preview (sample data)
screenshots.state: Codex reset · confirmation preview, not executed
screenshots.caption: Preview/confirm is separately gated. This fixture stops at the confirmation preview; the confirm button is visible but was never clicked, and no reset was redeemed.

rendered_text_assertions: Confirm reset on Codex Plus · sample

notes: All provider names, balances, windows, reset times, model names, and account labels are synthetic sample data.

Provider Usage targets stock Hermes Desktop 0.23.1+. Optional identity, reset, and delegated-owner metadata is capability-detected; when absent, the UI shows Unavailable/Unknown and provider dashboard links instead of a guessed value.
These component-harness captures use the current production renderer with synthetic usage figures. Unsupported stock xAI usage is shown as unavailable.
The screenshots exercise a real chip -> popover interaction and the real renderer; they do not prove packaged-app integration or live provider calls.
